module.web_files.checks: Looks for the standard public files of the site: robots.txt, sitemap.xml and security.txt (security contact, RFC 9116).
module.web_files.fix:
Create the file `/.well-known/security.txt` (RFC 9116), served over HTTPS as `text/plain` in UTF-8. Two fields are mandatory: `Contact` (a `mailto:` address or https URL) and `Expires` (an ISO 8601 date, less than one year ahead).
Give a dedicated, monitored mailbox (an alias such as `security@example.com`, not a personal address); add `Preferred-Languages`, `Canonical` (the file's address) and `Policy` (your disclosure policy) as needed.
Set a calendar reminder to renew `Expires` before it passes: an expired file is treated as stale by researchers and tools.
Review `robots.txt`: it is public, so do not list sensitive paths (administration, backups) believing it hides them. Protect them with authentication or IP filtering, then remove the `Disallow` lines that reveal them.
Check that `sitemap.xml` only lists the pages you want public, and declare it in `robots.txt` with a `Sitemap:` line.
Check publication with `curl -si https://example.com/.well-known/security.txt`, then run the scan again.
module.web_files.fix_snippet:
# security.txt
Contact: mailto:security@example.com
Expires: 2027-06-30T23:00:00.000Z
Preferred-Languages: en, fr
Canonical: https://example.com/.well-known/security.txt
Policy: https://example.com/security-policy
module.web_files.title: Web files
module.web_files.why: security.txt tells researchers whom to notify about a vulnerability; robots.txt sometimes reveals sensitive paths thought to be hidden.
